_comment: Acceptance fixtures for prose-structure-critic. Each synthetic fixture is a draft.md plus, where the
case is about support or order, the outline.json the writer intended. Drafts are this repo's own
writing (no corpus file has headings), so unlike the fidelity set nothing here is a corpus copy;
the leave-one-out negatives below are corpus essays staged directly from the corpus at prepare time.
`scan_says` is the ECHO RULE's verdict (tests/structure-harness.mjs), re-derived by the selftest:
what a critic gets by parroting outline-scan. `class` is the disagreement geometry, not a severity:
A  scan quiet, critic quiet     - it does not manufacture findings from counts
B  scan flags, critic quiet     - it clears an over-flag (a coda, a scene break, a list) with a reason
C  scan flags, critic flags     - it names WHICH count costs the argument
D  scan quiet, critic flags     - it catches what counts cannot see: order and support, against the outline
B and D are the whole argument for the critic existing. The parrot's score is reported beside the critic's.
The leave-one-out essays all read REVISE under the echo rule: every human essay has an unmarked
within-section boundary somewhere. So the parrot scores 0 of 12 on the negatives, and the critic
must stay quiet where the counts are loud. That is the negative test, and it measures structure a
human writer found acceptable, not whether the critic finds the right gaps.
echo_rule: flagged when balance.max_ratio >= 3, balance.min_ratio <= 0.34, or any within-section paragraph boundary is unmarked

fixtures.name: n-technical-flat
fixtures.draft_does: Six short, uniform reference sections. Flat is correct in a reference document; a critic that calls it imbalanced is wrong.

fixtures.name: n-post-marked
fixtures.draft_does: A four-section post, one paragraph per section, every boundary a heading. Nothing for the scan to flag and nothing for the critic to add.

fixtures.name: n-chapter-scene-breaks
fixtures.draft_does: A fiction chapter with scene breaks. The scan flags an unmarked within-section boundary; the cut is deliberate and the critic must clear it.

fixtures.name: n-essay-second-reason
fixtures.draft_does: The intact essay with its own outline. The scan flags 'There is a second reason' as an unmarked boundary; it is an enumeration and the critic must clear it. Every outline claim has a filled slot and the order matches.

fixtures.name: n-listicle-cuts
fixtures.draft_does: Five independent tips under one heading, each paragraph a fresh imperative. Four unmarked boundaries and a long section; all by design, none a gap.

fixtures.name: p-essay-orphan-claim
fixtures.draft_does: The load-bearing claim (the check must be mechanical) sits alone in a one-sentence section, ratio 0.12; its evidence is stranded in the objection section. The scan flags imbalance; the critic must say this one matters.

fixtures.name: p-essay-topic-jump
fixtures.draft_does: A paragraph about the writer's grandmother's bees interrupts an argument about calibration bands, with no link in or out. The scan flags two unmarked boundaries; the critic must name the jump, not the enumeration-like one.

fixtures.name: p-essay-unsupported
fixtures.draft_does: Every boundary is marked and the sections are balanced, so the scan is quiet. But outline claim n2 has an empty evidence slot and the draft states it as settled ('eliminates stale plan entries entirely… This is settled'). Only the outline exposes it.

fixtures.name: p-post-reordered
fixtures.draft_does: The post with its three corrections in the reverse of the outline's order: the lock section, which the outline places third because it depends on the thin-bands point, now comes first. Counts are quiet; only the outline exposes it.

leave_one_out_note: Twelve argumentative human essays: the four longest by Chesterton, Bacon and Doctorow in the licensed corpus. Staged draft-only (no outline exists for them), so classes 1 and 2 are not assessed and the critic's rule is silence on uncertainty. Expected CLEAN on all twelve; <= 2 REVISE is a default, not a measurement (critic-harness.md).
